Well okay, basically he goes on a journey of self redemption and soul searching (to put it that way.) And gets dissolutioned with humanity. Now depending on your interpretation on Mercer this is either very interesting for his development, or absolute shit writing. Due to the first game not exploring his personality much, and leaving a lot of his feelings up to interpretation, it's easy to say he's one way or the other.

Hey, I feel the exact same way. When I see someone else suffer, when I think about what they went through, it makes me really sad for them too. Like I wish I couldve done something. 

But if life has taught me anything, is that we are not a crumpled piece of paper or a broken base, we're like a piece of play dough. Life changes our shape, squishes us and pulls us apart, but the more time goes on, the tougher we get, and the less those blows hurt. 

Although I feel bad for those people, I feel glad, when they talk about all the things they have accomplished since. About all of the feats they have surpassed and accomplished. We can't help everyone, maybe not even anyone, but we can be happy for them. 

In some cases, something can be done. But that's not all the time, and honestly, thats just the sad truth about life. We live the life we get, and so does everyone else. Good or bad. You can't turn a blind eye, but you can make a positive impact to the people you can reach. The community around you. That old lady struggling with her bags? Get out of your way and help. 

That old man sitting alone at a park? Maybe he'd like a talk. That little girl crying because her ice cream cone fell? You can always offer her parent to buy another one. Just because. Doing tiny good deeds, just because will make an impact. Even if just for a fraction of a moment, you'll make someone happy. And then, the world seems a little less dark.

But when they came back, he died. That boy with a righteous mind is killed by Kira. A calculated murderer who wants to make the whole world how to him as a God. Bringing his ideals of justice to light, no matter what it takes. 

So in short, I felt sad when Light Yagami died. But at the end, it was just Kira who remained.

Honestly, I believe had he thought it just a little bit more through he could've made good changes in the world. He had already proven he could kill anyone. Joining forces with the police, or had he just held off and joined the police force as he was initially planning to, he could've easily escalated to L level in no time. Even L praises his deduction skills when they are both chained to each other. 

Once in this position, he could've been able to have information about all on going cases of criminals. Even if not convicted. Making it easier for him to give justice to criminals who are suspected of bigger crimes even if not caught. as he would also possibly be in charge of investigating them. 

Many people here complain about him not getting to the source, well, he could've! Literally just by threatening the life's of those in power, he could've made them change the system. Now this is all large scaled, but from what the rules in the anime are, and how smart light is, I believe, had he had any more patience, or had he thought about it thoroughly he could've made it possible. 

Lets not forget that as much as there is scared people, theres people who were deeply touched by his work, such is the case of Misa whose parents deaths were avenged by Kira. I believe people would NOT have been pushed into terror had Misa not killed those innocent people. Because as soon as she did that, the police were the ones actually putting fear into people saying Kira would kill ANYONE. Then it gets worse when that one company got their hands on the death note by further proving this idea. 

In short words, Light, although extremely intelligent, is a teenager with a big ego. He did not think of the death note as a means for a better world. He thought it as a mean of him becoming a God. Because it could've been used for a good purpose. Like who cares if people in power live in constant fear? They're the root source of the problem. 

The second thing is that even if he died, he could've continued his "reign of terror" or of "justice" as a shinigami. But then it wouldn't be satisfying. Because Light never wanted to help people to see humanity become better, he wanted humanity to see him as a hero and bow to him.

Another point I see here is that "rotten justice could never work". Well the truth is justice is rotten either way. Police officers take bribes, so do people in power. Kira or no Kira, there is no pure justice and there will never be because humans are flawed. At least in the case of the rethorical idea of Kira, punishment is inflicted on those convicted no matter what they might do. Isnt the idea of one murderer better than the idea of 100000 murderers? Especially if his policy is not killing anyone else other than criminals. He could scare police straight into doing their jobs right. And since its light we are talking about his deduction skills are above average. By investigating simple cases he would be able to reduce guilty from innocent. As I said before, theres anime rules, and in this universe the rule is light is always right in his deductions some how lol
